meta.notes: Edges filtered: reference===65 AND type==='bechina'. 10 bechina edges yielding 15 unique nodes across 5 raw connected components. Components D and E (two isolated pairs sharing the suffering/saltiness/thirst domain) merged into one package. Final result: 4 packages covering all 15 nodes.

packages.label: תַּכְלִית וּבִטּוּל
packages.reason: The dominant hub תכלית (the ultimate purpose/goal of all existence) is directly equated with four parallel concepts that illuminate the same reality from different angles: בטול (self-nullification — the experiential state of dissolving into the infinite), כלו טוב (all-is-good — the moral dimension: from the vantage of the takhlit, everything is revealed as pure good), אחד (Oneness — the metaphysical dimension: ה' is One and His name is One), and עדן (the Garden of Eden — the eschatological/spatial name for the place no eye has seen). These five nodes are all expressions of the same transcendent reality. In Torah #65, Rebbe Nachman builds his central teaching around this concept: the takhlit is both the eschatological endpoint AND the perspective that dissolves all suffering. The good/evil mirror is visible: the opposite of takhlit is the condition of eyes-open to this-world's vanity, where suffering is felt as total — but that negative pole is handled through eitza connections, not bechina ones. This cluster is entirely in the domain of holiness and the divine perspective.

packages.label: שִׂמְחָה וְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה
packages.label_en: Joy and the Receiving of Torah
packages.reason: The three nodes in this component share the same essential domain: the joyful, wholehearted commitment expressed at Sinai as 'נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִשְׁמַע' (we will do and we will hear). All three are aspects of the same spiritual act and state: שמחה (joy) IS a bechina of נעשה ונשמע because the Gemara (Shabbat 88a) teaches that when Israel said נעשה ונשמע, 600,000 angels placed two crowns on their heads, and those crowns are called 'שמחת עולם' — eternal joy. The שמחה is not the cause of the מעשה; it IS the character of the act of acceptance. Similarly, נעשה ונשמע IS a bechina of קבלת התורה — it is the defining moment and mode of Torah-receiving. This cluster describes the essential nature of joyful Torah-reception. In the Torah's argument, שמחה serves as the vessel (כלי) for receiving chidushei Torah — the joy that comes from seeing all sufferings as good generates the crown-state that enables Torah novelty to flow. This is the positive renewal dimension of the teaching.

packages.label: נֶפֶשׁ
packages.reason: The three nodes in this component are all aspects of the same dimension: the nefesh as the faculty of speech, prayer, and song. נפש is the central hub: רות is explicitly stated to BE a bechina of the nefesh ('למה נקרא שמה רות שממנה יצא דוד שריוה להקב"ה בשירות ותשבחות') — Ruth's essential nature is the soul-faculty that produces the songs and praises that satisfy the Divine. גן is also explicitly stated to be a bechina of the nefesh ('גן הוא בחינת הנפש, בחינת והיתה נפשם כגן רווה') — the garden-soul is the refreshed, watered soul. In Torah #65, the nefesh is the direct source of speech in prayer: the dibur (word) emerges from the nefesh (בראשית 2:7 — ויהי האדם לנפש חיה = לרוח ממללא). This cluster describes the essential nature of the nefesh as speech-origin and prayer-source — the figure of Ruth personifies it, and the garden-image captures its state of flourishing.

packages.label: יִסּוּרִין וְצִמְאוֹן הַנֶּפֶשׁ
packages.label_en: Suffering and the Thirst of the Soul
packages.reason: This package is formed by merging two small isolated pairs (Component D: מליחות ↔ יסורין; Component E: הרגשת היסורין ↔ צמאון הנפש) because they share the same essential bechina-nature and the source text explicitly chains them together: 'הַרְגָּשַׁת הַיִּסּוּרִין הוּא בְּחִינַת צִמְאוֹן הַנֶּפֶשׁ, כִּי צִמָּאוֹן הוּא עַל יְדֵי מְלִיחוּת, וּמְלִיחוּת הוּא בְחִינַת יִסּוּרִין'. This creates a direct bechina-chain: יסורין = מליחות = צמאון = הרגשת היסורין. All four describe the same phenomenological reality — suffering as experienced by the soul — from different angles: the covenantal dimension (ברית במלח = ברית ביסורין), the physical sensation (saltiness causing thirst), the experiential name (thirst of the soul), and the direct sensory description (felt-suffering). Polarity is neutral because in this Torah, suffering is neither intrinsically good nor evil — it is the domain of divine refinement that from the perspective of the takhlit is revealed as pure good, but as experienced in the moment is the painful starting-point the teaching addresses. It is a neutral object that can be transformed.

merge_notes.reason: This isolated pair shares the same bechina-nature as Component D (יסורין/מליחות). The source text in section ד explicitly chains them: הרגשת היסורין = צמאון הנפש, because צמאון is caused by מליחות, and מליחות IS יסורין. All four nodes describe the same experiential domain of suffering-as-thirst-and-saltiness. They are NOT cause-effect (it is not that מליחות produces צמאון — it IS צמאון by nature). Merged into this package by shared bechina-nature, not by eitza.

D and E share the same bechina-nature (suffering-as-salt-and-thirst) and the source text explicitly chains them into one bechina-sequence.
